clue.text: They open possibilities for new convert

indicators.note: possibilities suggests other ways of arranging these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh options are said to open the door to someone just converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibilities' is the anagram signal: the letters of THEY OPEN rearrange to give the answer, and 'for' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or someone newly received into a religion.

clue.text: Canter round for a drink

indicators.note: round suggests the letters of canter being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse canters round a field before stopping for refreshment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals rearranging the six letters of CANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods in Greek myth, and now any delicious drink.

clue.text: Love the navy, consumed by it …fancy!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at loving a navy that has been swallowed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by it' is padding that links the pieces; the definition 'fancy' is the adjective meaning elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate decoration is elaborate, the sense of fancy as opposed to plain.

clue.text: A Roman author with a little house and a lot of descendants

parts.note: HO is the short form of house, as on maps and addresses
a race is a line of people descended from common ancestors

explanation.surface: A Roman writer living in a small home with a big family.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a Latin lyric poet of the Augustan age.

clue.text: Check on rags and everything is ending

indicators.note: is ending says the word for everything comes last, after the rags

parts.note: tatters are torn rags
everything means all

explanation.surface: Inspecting worn rags when everything is coming to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: Tattersall is a check pattern of crossing lines on light cloth, named after a London horse market; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattersall is a fabric with a regular check pattern, so the word names a kind of check.

clue.text: Let out a belch and turn white!

indicators.note: let out suggests the letters being released and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone burps and goes pale with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' is read as freeing the letters of A BELCH to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach is to whiten or lose colour.

clue.text: He's in charge of provisions and stuff — regiment, about turn!

parts.note: to lard is to stuff or enrich meat with fat

indicators.note: the parade-ground order about turn means face the other way, so the two short pieces are read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
re is Latin for about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A quartermaster bellows an about-turn at the regiment while in charge of stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about turn' is a parade-ground order to face the other way, so it reverses the two short pieces, making ERER; the Royal Engineers is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A larderer was the officer of a household who looked after the larder and its stores.

clue.text: Marine seen out with Marian, holding each other

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the name being put out of order

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A marine is spotted on a date with a woman called Marian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the name into ARMINA; 'seen' and 'with' are link words, and the Royal Marine abbreviation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking arm in arm means linking arms, a way of holding one another.

clue.text: Rick, you might lose the point here!

definitions.text: Rick, you might lose the point here!

parts.words: Rick, you might lose the point here!
parts.note: a rick is a stack of hay, and the point you lose is a needle, as in the proverb about searching for one

explanation.surface: Someone warns Rick he could miss the point of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a man's name addressed in the clue; it is a stack of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a large stack of hay, the proverbial place to lose a needle.

clue.text: Sorry to cheat with a corny ending

parts.note: to con is to swindle
trite means hackneyed or stale, coming at the end

explanation.surface: Apologising for swindling, with a clichéd finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' puts TRITE last; 'to' and 'with a' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling remorse, penitent for a wrong done.

clue.text: Add a little weight to first person's record award

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
my is the first-person possessive

explanation.surface: Advice to pile a few grams onto your own record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grammys are the annual American awards for recorded music.

clue.text: An indefinite example of such things

definitions.text: An indefinite example of such things

parts.words: An indefinite example of such things
parts.note: the clue's first word, An, is itself the indefinite one of the grammatical words a, an and the

explanation.surface: A vague sample of some unspecified items.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'An' reads as a mere article; it is the example being described.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a, an and the are the determiners called by this name, a and an being indefinite.

clue.text: Return money to jelly-maker

indicators.note: return asks for the money word to be sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Asking a jam-maker to refund the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet curdles milk, setting it into junket, a milk jelly.

clue.text: Naughty timmy and I have spoken of sinfulness

indicators.note: have means the shuffled letters hold the spoken word inside them
naughty suggests the letters of timmy and I misbehaving into a new order

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A naughty boy called Timmy and the speaker have talked about sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' scrambles the boy's name and I into IMMITY, and 'have' places the spoken word inside it; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Immorality is wickedness, behaviour against moral principles.

clue.text: When first young men use measuring system, the result is irregular

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the metric system is a system of measurement

explanation.surface: Once young men adopt the metric system, things become lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' picks Y and M from 'young men'; 'use' and 'the result is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetric means lacking symmetry, so uneven or lopsided.

clue.text: Provision of meals needing a hundred sinks

indicators.note: needing says the meals must take in the hundred to be complete

parts.note: suppers are evening meals provided
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Serving dinners that call for a hundred places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinks' looks like the noun for kitchen basins; it is the verb, and scuppers are also deck drains.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a ship is to sink it deliberately, and scuppers also drain water from a deck.

clue.text: An engine part having many features

explanation.definitionFit: A manifold is the branched pipe carrying gases in an engine; manifold also means many and varied.

clue.text: Account firm restricts Paul badly when in Mexican resort

indicators.note: restricts means the two abbreviations hem in the jumbled name

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: badly suggests the name Paul written wrongly

explanation.surface: An accountancy firm limits Paul's behaviour on a Mexican trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the name into APUL, and 'restricts' hems it between the two abbreviations; 'when in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a beach resort city on Mexico's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Minister must gamble pounds sterling against gold

parts.note: a chance is a risk or gamble
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra
L also stands for sterling, the pound
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A government minister bets money against gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Chancellor of the Exchequer is the finance minister; 'must' and 'against' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the British cabinet minister in charge of finance.

clue.text: Money we almost all need at the end of the month

indicators.note: almost means the word all is cut short by its final letter
at the end of the points to the closing pair of letters of the word month

explanation.surface: We all need money by the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL; 'at the end of the' takes the last two letters of 'month'; 'need' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is riches, an abundance of money and possessions.

clue.text: Fish that is supplied the least at present

parts.note: min is short for minimum, the least
now means at present

explanation.surface: A fish handed out in the smallest amount just now.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a small freshwater fish.

clue.text: Rodents retreating from the line of heavenly bodies

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the rodents are read in reverse

parts.note: rats are rodents
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the line

explanation.surface: Rodents scurry back from the railway line under the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; the definition is an adjectival phrase, matching starry.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry describes things relating to or full of stars.

clue.text: "Titivates" is written in second footnote around the edge

indicators.note: around means the second footnote is wrapped round the edge

parts.note: PPS is a second postscript added to a letter
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A word is written into the second footnote round the page margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is written in' is a link; titivate means to smarten oneself up.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom or smarten oneself fussily.

clue.text: Look forward to a raise — it could take years off you!

definitions.text: it could take years off you!

parts.note: to face is to look forward towards something
a lift is a raise

explanation.surface: Looking forward to a pay rise that might make you feel younger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' looks like a pay rise; it is a lift. The definition is cryptic: cosmetic surgery takes years off your looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery to tighten facial skin makes a person look younger.

clue.text: French star injured toe — lie about it

indicators.note: injured suggests the letters of toe and lie being knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A French celebrity hurts her toe and lies down about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges TOE and LIE together; 'about it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Etoile is French for star, used for a leading ballet dancer.

clue.text: Hatter taking measure for boater?

explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes hats, so measures heads for a straw boater.

clue.text: Team at play appear in profile

parts.note: a side is a team
on means in progress or playing, as a match that is on

explanation.surface: The team on the field look good from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen side-on means seen from the side, in profile.

clue.text: Incidentally, it could be on the verge

definitions.text: it could be on the verge

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means by chance as a conversational aside; literally, something at the roadside is beside the road, on its grass verge.
